rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Per this task's explicit instruction, §3 is evaluated against the maintainer block too. The pinned diff (4a722813..HEAD) touched the maintainer block only to swap 'is ceremony' -> 'adds nothing' (removing a hard-banned word, not adding history) and bump the Quality-line SHAs (structured freshness metadata, exempt). Closest candidate to a journey-clause: L86 'When `cohort-onboarding-email.md` was collapsed into a welcome plus a link here, two of its sections had no other home: confirming a paid Claude licence is active, and confirming a corp proxy or VPN is not in the way.' Reads as a transition verb ('was collapsed') but stays inside the rule: it supplies the referent for the next sentence's 'neither is owed' (without it, 'neither' names nothing), matching the rule's own keepable category ('an empirical finding that would otherwise be re-derived') rather than idle changelog. The clause that follows it -- 'Do not add a setup beat for either, and do not resolve it by restoring the email, which would re-open the drift the collapse closed.' -- is a licensed do-not-reintroduce clause. L88's 'Accepted-by-design 2026-08-13 (Antti-directed): do not extract, do not re-raise' is the same dated-provenance + standing-constraint shape. No 'was changed to' / 'renamed from' / 'restored after' / 'used to' construction anywhere in the block. Body-region dated_line grep (CLEAN, planted-proof true, 0 hits in lines 1-83) confirms no stale marker in body prose itself.

No flinch phrases from the write-to-the-caution list ('just a simple', 'trust the agent', 'leash', 'niceness'). Grep for 'vendor' -- 0 hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat -- the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: L15 '**Trivial bug**, wanted on day one: a few lines here and there.' is a bold-label-plus-colon definition-list item, not the banned bold-label-echo shape (the elaboration doesn't restate 'Trivial bug' as its own grammatical subject -- contrast the rule's counter-example '**Acceptance Tests.** Acceptance tests define...'). Same shape at L16-18 for the other three sizes. No empty negation (L18's 'not counting the time you spend writing prompts' clarifies a genuine ambiguity, not a guessed-Y). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.

L13's lede 'Roughly in the order you'll reach for them:' carries the ordering once; L15's 'wanted on day one' is the rule's own named survivor example beneath it (a real deadline the sequence alone can't state), quoted near-verbatim in the compendium itself. L30's 'Real work ahead at two sizes... The repo should have both' is prose describing two content categories, not a numeral sitting beside a visible bulleted list -- distinct from this rule's targeted shape (adjacent-to-a-list), so not filed here; noted as a close call rather than a violation since the rule's own wording (bullets, adjacent list) doesn't clearly reach it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No abstract-twin restatement (each paragraph states its point once, at one altitude). No widening-qualifier hedge ('or context-dependent'). Body lead-ins next to the {{prompt:}} blocks (L45, L60, L66) summarise rather than restate the fences' full content -- they name what's about to happen without re-listing the fences' own screening criteria or step numbers. L32 'Pick one. Every rule and every memory you build during the training lands here.' is the rule's own ideal survivor shape: concrete instance + one generalising sentence, then stop.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'you already think X' / "you're missing Y" corrective-gap language. Grep for ability-tier phrasing ('at your scale', 'for a beginner', 'once you're more experienced', 'a senior would already know') -- 0 hits. No tourist/practitioner-style identity criterion present. The readiness check (L58-66: repo can test/branch/commit/PR) and the GitHub-CLI check (L22) are both plausibly-failable for this audience at this point. The maintainer's L86 accept-note is itself evidence of this rule's plausibly-failable test being actively applied: the licence and network checks were removed precisely because they fail the diagnostic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.

Model/thinking-effort terms (L3-5: /model, Sonnet, Opus, thinking effort) are explained in the same blockquote where they're used. L29's 'somewhere with enough surface area for rules and memory to land on' is the anticipatory-unfold technique this rule's carve-out (a) names almost verbatim -- 'rules and memory' as curriculum-load-bearing nouns are not yet authored by the student in prework, so previewed rather than earned-as-abstract-noun is correct. L16's 'Plan mode' and L22's 'gh'/GitHub CLI are Claude-Code/industry-standard terms an AE101 engineer audience already carries (assumed-known carve-out, parallel to MCP/connector/CI/PR/repo).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body -- THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L34 'Really stuck for a repo that fits? Ask your trainer for the fallback repo...' is a what-if-X-fails branch correctly kept in body under the rule's own named exception (plausible failure + non-obvious rescue). L66's AskUserQuestion fallback ('If the agent's screening feels like everything-at-once...') is the same shape: plausible failure (agent behaviour variance) + non-obvious rescue, correctly kept in body since it's needed live, mid-session, and the maintainer fence would delete it for both trainer and student in delivery.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompt over-specifies output structure. The bug-screen prompt's explicit screening criteria (under 50 lines, visible, mine/co-owned, shippable) are substantive teaching content, not incidental formatting. All four fences (verified via `node scripts/expand-md.js`) end with a plain 'report/tell me what you did' ask rather than a prescribed document shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L62 'push back if it dumps all four criteria at once' -- actor (student), mechanism (push back), object (the agent's bug-screen, anchored by the preceding clause), tell ('dumps all four criteria at once') are all present. L66 fallback names actor+mechanism+object+tell equally clearly ('ask Claude to use the AskUserQuestion tool, or ... one bug at a time'). No teacher-verb 'name' smell (grep for 'name the'/'names the' -- 0 hits). No speech verb (say/name/call/quote/tell/flag) lacking an explicit addressee in body prose (grep confirms the only 'flag'/'call' hits are HTML build-comments and the idiom 'Your call.'). No unfounded-diagnosis or unreachable-criterion construction found; L62's 'a few lines here and there' criterion is made concrete by the fence's own '<50 lines changed'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.

'Pre-read before Module 1' is a reading-list-style header naming the section's type (established convention across the AE101 corpus's several 'Pre-read(s) before Module N' sections, per this rule's own §33 cross-reference), not a vague topic-noun header of the banned kind ('The repo', 'Content folder'). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself -- subject test, then deletion test.

Deletion test on remaining candidates: L11's real-work framing and L26's repo-decision framing both pass with the student's own artifact/decision as subject; L30's 'Later the training runs experiments on bigger things' has 'the training' as grammatical subject, which trips the letter of the subject test, but its predicate (naming what 'bigger things' means: an epic, a refactor, a feature with unknowns) is load-bearing for the immediately-following 'The repo should have both' -- deleting it breaks that sentence's referent rather than joining cleanly, so it fails the rule's own deletion test for a cut. Flagged as a phrasing note (todos), not a violation: the content is decision-relevant now, only the subject noun is avoidable.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer note documents the design intent directly: 'No pre-fabricated files. Student generates all state in conversation... the manual-download fallback is a transport primitive, not a file-edit.' The tarball/skills setup is trainer-authored transport the student wouldn't hand-produce (a curated STRIDE skill, access-control-analysis skill) -- the legitimate scaffold exception this rule names.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.

Yes -> setup, not teaching') applies cleanly to the whole file. Statable transition: student leaves prework equipped and mildly anticipatory, set up for Module 1's opening icebreaker question (L82). No verification/check-the-URL step prematurely resolves a later doubt-beat's mood.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.

Extract the bundle and install the curated skills') carries the command verb and object, which discharges the requirement under §2c ('A `##` header carrying the command verb IS the lead-in', Antti 2026-08-30) -- and this exact file/section is the rule's own named calibration example for that carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape -- lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four prompt blocks (verified via `node scripts/expand-md.js curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md`) render exactly `**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*` followed by a blank line then the fence. No 'copy ->' prefix, no '(end of prompt)' closer, no blockquote/backtick/naked-indent wrapping.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation -- don't leak downstream pipeline.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Question-dump default -- `in turn` too soft; two legal shapes.

Whichever reads better.') as a rescue if the structural instruction still batches -- belt-and-suspenders, exceeding the rule's bar.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action -- design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Both multi-step prompts (extract+install; bug-screen) carry an explicit in-fence 'no preamble' directive in their opening sentence. The single-step download prompt doesn't need one and doesn't have one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.

(extract+install; bug-screen). No pre-confirm-before-acting pattern present; none of these actions are irreversible/high-stakes enough to need the carve-out anyway.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` -- custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four expand to exactly `**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*`, no custom label variant.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1's request ('Download the AE101 content tarball to `~/Downloads/ae101-content.tar.gz` using curl.') is a direct request with no unnecessary orchestration preamble. P3's structured screening criteria are protocol that IS the lesson (the rule's own named exception), not orchestration bloat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.

Verified the four registry files exist at `curriculum/prompts/ae101-prework-{download-tarball,extract-and-install,screen-and-ready,one-at-a-time}.md`.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.

None depend on body-only context to execute correctly.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move -- paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The download fence splits its three moves (download+report / auth conditional / URL) into three paragraphs. The extract+install and bug-screen fences split their moves via numbered list items (1./2./3. and 1./2.). No wide single-paragraph instruction-stream present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The pinned diff (4a722813..HEAD) fixed the download prompt's mismatch: L45 now reads 'Ask Claude to download `ae101-content.tar.gz`...', matching the fence's own opening 'Download the AE101 content tarball...' verb-for-verb.
